newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Danish-Swedish link to borrow 4 bln DKK in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Danish-Swedish link to borrow 4 bln DKK in 1997.

text.p: The Danish-Swedish consortium building a bridge and tunnel link between the two countries says it expects to have borrowed about 19 billion crowns ($3 billion) by the time the project is completed in the year 2000.

In a briefing at a construction site on the narrow Oeresund channel dividing the Swedish port of Malmo from the Danish capital, Copenhagen, Oeresundskonsortiet CEO Sven Landelius said eight billion crowns had so far been raised on capital markets and 1997 issuance should add four billion crowns.

"We raise in different currencies, and our currency basket consists mainly of Danish crowns, Swedish crowns, marks, French francs, Swiss francs, guilders and a small proportion, about four percent, in yen," he told reporters on Tuesday.

Owned jointly by the Danish and Swedish states, who guarantee its debt, the consortium is rated AAA by Standard and Poor and was among the first to issue the popular four-percent bond when the Danish coupon floor was lowered last October.

The separate Oeresundsforbindelsen company, responsible for road and rail links and other infrastructure on the Danish side, has also been a keen user of the four-percent Danish crown bond, issuing so far at least 1.35 billion crowns of varying maturity.

Costs for the entire project, including infrastructure on the Swedish side, are projected at 21 billion Danish crowns at current prices, and Landelius said that the project was so far both on budget and on time.
Favourable currency movements, he added, had made the cost of borrowing minimal.

"We have had a good time from the finance markets. Our costs for financing during 1996, excluding currency, are a little bit more than 3.12 percent and including currency, they are below one percent."
The costs of the project are to be covered by tolls on the 10,000 vehicles expected to cross daily, and debt is to be repaid after about 25 years of operation.
Unlike the Anglo-French channel tunnel, there are no private shareholders in the first fixed link between Denmark and Sweden. Any loss would be borne by taxpayers.

Journey time to Malmo from central Copenhagen will be about 15 minutes, compared to at least 90 minutes for the shortest car ferry route at present. --Copenhagen newsroom +45 33969650 ($ = 6.433 Danish Crowns)
